title: Session 2 — Participant 43 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Build and validate a simple automated monthly hotel KPI dashboard that summarizes financial and operating performance and highlights the main variances for management review.
context: For Session 2, I will build a simple monthly hotel KPI dashboard using anonymized financial and operating data. This is different from Session 1, which focused on cash flow and owner funding. The difficulty is similar, but the objective is simpler: organize the data, calculate a small group of hotel KPIs, identify the main variances, and prepare a short management summary. In Session 1 I used Claude selectively; in Session 2 I will use Claude in every step for data review, KPI definitions, Excel formulas, interpretation, and final validation.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: The dashboard was completed and validated as planned.

Step 1.step_name: Review and organize the source data
Step 1.step_action: Review the anonymized monthly P&L and operating data and identify the fields needed for the dashboard. Use Claude to help organize the data, flag missing or inconsistent information, and confirm which source lines should feed each KPI.

nodes.label: Open the workbook and frame the dashboard goal
nodes.detail: Opens the 'Minesota' workbook (a new P&L exercise for the same hotel and winery entity as Session 1, figures in Mexican pesos) and explains the goal of building a single-tab KPI dashboard comparing actuals, budget, and prior year.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to translate the Spanish source data
nodes.detail: Notes the source data is in Spanish and asks Claude to translate the visible sheets into English before building the dashboard.

nodes.label: Catalog the Spanish text into a unique-string list
nodes.detail: Scans the visible sheets (KPI's, LY, Actuals, FBudget, Actuals+F, DepartamentalNS, Clasificacion), extracts roughly 3,760 text cells, and reduces them to 504 unique Spanish strings to translate.

nodes.label: Stop Claude and hide unnecessary data in Excel
Ask to continue previous task
Build, apply, and verify the Spanish-to-English translation map
nodes.detail: Builds a Spanish-to-English translation map for the 504 unique strings and applies it across all visible sheets' non-formula text cells, leaving proper nouns (Casa 8, Casa Montana, El Atico) and month names untouched, then re-reads the sheets to confirm no formula errors were introduced before the participant moves on.

nodes.label: Check the translation

Step 2.step_name: Select the KPIs and dashboard structure
Step 2.step_action: Select a small set of hotel KPIs for the dashboard, such as occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, total revenue, GOP, and GOP margin. Use Claude to confirm the KPI definitions and formulas and to suggest a simple layout that shows actual, budget, prior year, and variance.

nodes.label: Build the column-block layout for the dashboard
nodes.detail: On the KPI's tab, builds by hand an Actuals/%/Budget/%/Var($)/Var(%) block for the current month, then a second LY/%/Var($)/Var(%) block, formatting the LY header with an orange fill.

nodes.label: Lay out the full KPI row list
nodes.detail: Lays out the full row list of KPIs down column B: Key Statistics (Available Rooms, Occupied Rooms, %Ocup., Average Rate, RevPar), Revenues (Rooms, F&B, Winery, Other, Total Revenue), Cost of Sales, Fixed Expenses, GOP, EBITDA, Other Expenses, and Net Income.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to confirm the U.B.O. definition
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to confirm the position and definition of 'U.B.O.' (Utilidad Bruta de Operacion, Spanish for Gross Operating Profit) in the P&L hierarchy.

nodes.label: Trace the U.B.O. formula and flag it as equivalent to G.O.P.
nodes.detail: Traces the underlying formula (Total Revenue minus Total Costs minus Fixed Expenses) and flags that the same metric appears elsewhere as G.O.P./Gross Operating Profit, asking whether to harmonize the label.

nodes.label: Check the rows in Excel and edit the lay out
Ask whether have any #REFS
Scan for #REF!/#DIV/0! errors from deleted tabs and propose fixes
nodes.detail: In parallel, scans the sheets for #REF!/#DIV/0! errors that appeared after the DepartamentalNS and Clasificacion tabs were deleted, isolating 9 #REF! cells (row 204, a Total AVG Rate row with a broken lookup) and 7 #DIV/0! cells (row 65, a divide-by-zero that will self-resolve once a denominator row is populated), and proposes a fix for each.

nodes.label: Review and adjust the worksheet structure

Step 3 + 4.step_name: Build the KPI calculations in Excel and Review variances and identify key insights
Step 3 + 4.step_action: Build Excel formulas that calculate the selected KPIs and variances versus budget and prior year. Use Claude to suggest formulas, troubleshoot any errors, and check that the calculations update correctly when the source data changes.

nodes.label: Prompt Claude to pull December Actuals via lookup
nodes.detail: Prompts Claude, based on the active Month-selector cell (C2), to pull the December Actuals into the KPI's tab's Current Month Actuals column, refining the prompt for precision after an initial vague attempt.

nodes.label: Generate KPI lookup formulas, populate Current Month Actuals, and catch data issues
nodes.detail: Runs an INDEX/MATCH-style lookup matching each KPI row label against the corresponding Actuals line, populating column B with real figures (Total Revenue 4,992,609; GOP -588,149; EBITDA -898,228; Net Income -2,119,702, among others). Flags four rows intentionally left blank because they have no direct Actuals equivalent (Payroll-Operations splits across Hotel/Winery/Maintenance; Cost of Sales/Operating Expenses department-split issue; Winery Cost-CVG; Fixed Expenses/FX Fluctuation) and asks how to aggregate them. Detects that the Actuals month-header cell read "DICIEMBRE" (reintroduced in Spanish by an earlier column insert) instead of "DECEMBER", breaking the month match, and fixes it. Finds the Actuals row labelled "Total Available Rooms" actually held a per-day rooms figure (33) rather than the true period total (1,023) living on an unlabeled row, and flags it with a cell note instead of silently overwriting it.

nodes.label: Evaluate the populated figures and blank-row decisions
nodes.detail: Reviews the populated Actuals figures and the four intentionally-blank rows, weighing Claude's proposed aggregation approach.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to rebuild the P&L with the new segmentation
nodes.detail: Types a request in the Claude sidebar to resume/rebuild the P&L so every line reflects the new Hotel/Winery/Non-Operating expense segmentation with correct figures throughout, rather than continuing to hand-extend the lookup formulas herself.

nodes.label: Diagnose segmentation mismatch, restore the month-lookup driver, and reconcile Total Expenses
nodes.detail: Confirms the new Operating Expenses segmentation (Hotel/Winery/Non-Operating), maps each subtotal to its source row in Actuals, and finds the three segments alone don't tie to the reported Total Expenses. Separately discovers that the participant's own edits had cleared the KPI's C2 month-lookup driver, breaking the Z-column mapping; restores the driver and remaps the Z22:Z24 references for the new Hotel/Winery/Non-Operating segments. While reconciling subtotals, finds that Total Expenses still does not tie out — the Hotel + Winery + Non-Operating segments sum to less than the reported total by exactly an unassigned Cost of Sales/Other Revenue line — which it folds into the total and flags to the participant.

nodes.label: Check the segmentation mismatch and restore the cleared month-lookup driver
Ask to build column D and I
Diagnose the duplicate-label ambiguity for Other Expenses
nodes.detail: Discovers the 'Other Expenses' row's lookup was silently matching the wrong one of two identically-labeled 'Total Fixed Expenses' rows in the Actuals sheet (one for Advisory Fee/Lease, another later block for CapEx/Rent/D&A), and explains the ambiguity to the participant.

nodes.label: Check the output
Request Var($) and Var(%) formulas for the Current Month block
nodes.detail: Requests Var($) and Var(%) formulas for both the Actuals-vs-Budget and Actuals-vs-LY comparisons across every KPI row in the Current Month block. Review the KPI results and identify the largest positive and negative variances. Use Claude to help prioritize the most important changes, suggest possible explanations, and challenge the interpretation before I decide which insights are supported by the data.

nodes.label: Build, verify, and flag sign-convention nuances in IF-wrapped variance formulas
nodes.detail: Builds an IF-wrapped variance formula that returns a blank when either side of the comparison is empty (covering the four intentionally-unmapped rows from the earlier sub-phase), then verifies that dollar and percentage variances are correct and unambiguous on every row, noting that LY rows 22–24 (Hotel/Winery/Non-Operating expense splits) remain blank because LY has no equivalent departmental breakdown. While finishing the variance columns, proactively raises that on rows where the KPI itself is negative (GOP, EBITDA, Net Income), a percentage variance computed as Actuals/Comparator-1 can be misleading since a positive-looking ratio can represent a worse outcome, and walks through two concrete examples: GOP's LY variance shows +126% (looks favorable but is actually worse since both figures are negative and the ratio inverts), while EBITDA's LY variance shows -82.6% (looks unfavorable but represents a real improvement since the negative Actuals figure is much smaller in magnitude than the negative LY figure).

nodes.label: Evaluate Claude's variance results and consider handling misleading percentages
nodes.detail: Reviews Claude's variance formulas and sign-convention warning, then considers whether to suppress or flag potentially misleading percentages for negative-KPI rows.

Step 5.step_name: Validate the dashboard and prepare a short summary
Step 5.step_action: Check the main KPI calculations against the source data and prepare a concise summary of the most important results. Use Claude to review the calculations, identify any inconsistencies, and improve the clarity of the final management commentary.

nodes.label: Instruct Claude to repeat the structure for a Complete Year block
nodes.detail: Instructs Claude to repeat the same actuals/budget/LY/variance logic for a second 'Complete Year' block of columns, reusing the month-label helper map.

nodes.label: Build full-year lookups, apply LY unit conversion, and diagnose formula bugs
nodes.detail: Builds the full-year lookups and cross-checks the pulled Budget full-year figures directly against the FBudget tab's Jan–Dec summary, confirming Total Revenue and Profit Hotel/Winery subtotals match. Sums the LY tab's monthly columns with a ×1,000 unit conversion since LY is stored in thousands to build the LY full-year statistics. Discovers two full-year cells (Other Expenses and Net Income LY) returning wildly wrong values (-400,983,784 and +385,825,911), traces the issue to a stray text-space character in a source label plus a duplicate "Total Fixed Expenses" label being matched incorrectly, and begins correcting it as the recording ends but something went wrong.

nodes.label: Claude stops, adjust lay out and Excel data manually
